land.text: the Later Han realm less the Northern Han core round Taiyuan

predecessors.note: 'Founded by Guo Wei (Emperor Taizu), it was preceded by the Later Han dynasty.' Cliopatria's Later Han row (947-959) outlives the Later Han; the land is its outline minus Cliopatria's Northern Han shape.

land.text: the Later Zhou realm, taken over by Zhao Kuangyin's Song

successors.note: 'Soon thereafter, Zhao Kuangyin usurped the throne and declared himself emperor of the Great Song dynasty'; formal abdication 3 February 960. Cliopatria's Northern Song row begins in 961.

capitals.name: Kaifeng
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Kaifeng'; the page is silent on the name Dongjing.

rulers.name: Taizu (Guo Wei)
rulers.title: Emperor
rulers.note: Died of illness in 954, 'ended his three-year reign'.

rulers.name: Shizong (Chai Rong)
rulers.title: Emperor
rulers.note: Guo Wei's adoptive son; died 27 July 959 on campaign (Shizong page).

correction.text: Guo Wei's realm: the Later Han outline without the Northern Han core

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 951-957. Cliopatria has no Later Zhou shape before 960: its Later Han row (947-959, 790,319 km2, the same outline as the Later Jin 936 shape) is drawn through the whole Later Zhou reign although the Later Zhou page puts the dynasty's founding in 951. That outline still contains the Northern Han core (136 cells round Taiyuan, 111.1-113.8 E, 37.6-39.0 N), which Liu Min took out in 951 ('Liu Min founded the Northern Han Kingdom ... in 951', Northern Han page), so it is subtracted. The page gives no area to compare. The Later Shu prefectures (Qin, Feng, Cheng, Jie, 955) are not dated by any page opened; the Cliopatria outline already runs west to 104.5 E.

correction.text: the Later Zhou realm of 960 including Huainan, from 958

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 958-959: Cliopatria's 960 shape stretched back two years. It adds Huainan (678 cells, 114.3-121.8 E, 30.4-34.7 N), which Cliopatria carries as a 'Southern Wu' row to 959: 'The Later Zhou gained control over Huainan and almost a quarter million families'; 'Forced to cede Huainan and become a vassal of Later Zhou: 958'. The Yangtze line is the frontier ('cede all territory north of the Yangtze').

902,631 km2 for 960, one year only. Cliopatria's 960 shape is the Later Han outline minus the Northern Han core plus Huainan; the last month of the dynasty (3 February 960) is the shape's whole year, and Song's own row begins in 961. The page has no area. The Liao and Northern Han frontiers are not described on any page opened.

ledger.note: 951: Guo Wei proclaims the Later Zhou at Kaifeng. Lead: 'Guo Wei... declared himself emperor of the new Later Zhou on New Year's Day in 951'; infobox 'Dynasty established: 13 February 951' (the page does not reconcile the two, so month 2 follows the infobox). The region is Cliopatria's Later Han outline less Northern Han; the page names no frontier.

956: the Later Zhou invade Huainan. 'Later Zhou forces advanced south and constructed a floating bridge to cross the Huai River at Zhengyang' and 'began the invasion of Huainan in early 956'; Shouchun 'resisted them for 14 months'. The advice to strike came 'in spring 955'.

958: Shouchun falls and the Southern Tang yields. 'By April 958 Shouchun had fallen and the Later Zhou were advancing upon the capital of Jinling'; 'The Southern Tang offered to cede all territory north of the Yangtze to the Later Zhou and become a vassal.'

region.text: Huainan, 'all territory north of the Yangtze'

ledger.note: 958: Huainan passes to the Later Zhou. 'Li Jing was forced to become a vassal of the Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou, cede all territory north of the Yangtze River, and relinquish his title of emperor.' The Cliopatria shape that holds this land to 959 is labelled Southern Wu.

region.text: the Southern Tang south of the Yangtze

ledger.note: 958: the Southern Tang becomes a Later Zhou vassal. Infobox 'Forced to cede Huainan and become a vassal of Later Zhou: 958'; 'Tributes were paid to the Later Zhou once they defeated the Southern Tang in 958.' Li Jing took the title 'King of Tang' and Later Zhou called him 'King of Jiangnan'.

region.text: the Southern Tang south of the Yangtze

ledger.note: 960: the Southern Tang's vassalage passes to the Song. 'In 960, the Southern Tang became a vassal of the newly established Northern Song dynasty.'

960: the last Later Zhou emperor abdicates and the Song begins. Infobox 'Formal abdication: 3 February 960'; 'Soon thereafter, Zhao Kuangyin usurped the throne and declared himself emperor of the Great Song dynasty.' The Chen Bridge mutiny is not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Battle of Gaoping
wars.outcome: Chai Rong's army met Liu Chong's at Gaoping (Jincheng, Shanxi); two of Chai's generals fled and the Later Zhou won the day; no territory moved on the pages opened.
wars.note: 'When Chai Rong engaged Liu Chong at Gao Ping (in modern Jincheng, Shanxi)...'; 'After this campaign, Chai Rong consolidated his power.' The Northern Han page names its founder Liu Min and is silent on 954 and on Gaoping.

wars.name: Later Zhou conquest of Huainan
wars.outcome: Later Zhou took Huainan by 958; the Southern Tang ceded all land north of the Yangtze, dropped the imperial title and became a tributary.
wars.note: The page's Economy section says 'From 955 to 988 the Later Zhou successfully campaigned against the Southern Tang', evidently a typo for 958.

wars.name: Later Zhou pressure on the Northern Han and the Liao
wars.outcome: Shizong 'began putting pressure on the Northern Han and even the Liao dynasty, though nothing substantial came of it' before dying in 959; no border moved on the pages opened.
wars.note: The Three Passes and the Guannan prefectures, the 955 Later Shu prefectures and Wuyue, Jingnan and Chu relations are all 'page silent' on the Later Zhou, Shizong, Northern Han and Later Shu pages.

certainty.note: No frontier is described on any page opened. After 958 the Yangtze is the line the Southern Tang accepted ('cede all territory north of the Yangtze'), the nearest thing to a fixed border; the Northern Han, Liao and Later Shu frontiers are approximate.

notes: Split of the Cliopatria row 'Later Zhou' (-750..960): its 960 shape is this Five Dynasties dynasty (slug later-zhou, the Cliopatria slug kept); its five Eastern Zhou shapes are in eastern-zhou.json. Cliopatria lacks the dynasty for 951-959: the Later Han row (947..959) is drawn instead, so the Later Han dossier (ea-04) should end its Later Han shape at 950/951 and the keyframe later-zhou_951 here carries the land; 'Southern Wu' (Cliopatria) is still drawn on Huainan in 955-959 although the Southern Tang held it from 937 (page: founded 937, 'Overthrow of the Yang Wu dynasty: 937'). Page silent (so no events): the 954 Gaoping territorial result, the 955-956 Later Shu prefectures (Qin, Feng, Cheng, Jie), the number of Huainan prefectures ceded, the 959 Liao campaign and the Three Passes, the Chen Bridge mutiny, and the Wuyue, Jingnan, Min or Chu relations; the Cliopatria outline of 104.5 E to 122.6 E already includes the western prefectures. Date conflict: founding 'New Year's Day in 951' (lead) vs 13 February 951 (infobox); the Southern Tang page's '955 to 988' is a typo. Names: Northern Han's founder is Liu Min on its own page and Liu Chong on the Shizong page (one person). Budget: 5 pages (up to 5 allowed); the Later Shu page was silent. Wikidata Q1154556 is the Five Dynasties Later Zhou; the Eastern Zhou rows in the Cliopatria row share it by mistake.
